newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip in dead market, more falls feared.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip in dead market, more falls feared.

text.p: Danish share prices closed slightly higher on Wednesday in a market lacking interest or direction, with more falls foreseen up to the interim result season due to get underway next week.
"There's a dearth of market-moving news so interest flags and prices slip. Things should be better next week when a welter of major 1997 first-half results are due," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index lost 0.41 point to close at 184.76 in overall bourse turnover of 930 million crowns. The KFX August future fell 0.15 point to 185.05 with 183 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Foreign investors entered the market in the late afternoon, triggering some activity but the predominant mood was quiet, another dealer said.
SAS recovered from recent bouts of profit-taking to finish 2.5 crowns up at 102.50, while Carlsberg brewery shed 10 crowns to end at 344 on concern about its operations in Britain.
News of restructuring and the setting of a target to double turnover by 2000 failed to boost GN Store Nord, which closed 15 crowns down at 720.
